learning: Iteration 7 gave 14 of 20 oval completions with 16 mm sensors at ±0.06 m, while 12 mm gave none (iteration 8). The 16 mm footprint is necessary. Slalom line loss of 0.3 at 0.6 kg is the target. If line loss falls and oval completions hold, the wider span helps. If oval completions fall while line loss falls, rescale weights (for example to about 0.86 times) before changing geometry.
notes: Builder's ±0.07 m span on the iteration 7 platform, with gains and line-loss rule unchanged. Weights are proportional to x so the outer sensors stay at ±2.
rationale: Iteration 7 (16 mm, seven sensors at x = ±0.06 m, y = 0.02 m, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m body, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels, kp 2.2, kd 0.5) is the best race so far at 303.8, with 14 of 20 oval completions. Its s-bend and slalom still end off track, and slalom line_loss_events are 0.3. Iteration 8 showed that 12 mm sensors remove oval completions (0 of 20), so the 16 mm footprint stays. The Builder's proposal keeps 16 mm and widens the span to x = ±0.07 m at pitch about 0.0233 m, which tests outer-edge margin. Body, mass, track, wheel radius and row height (y = 0.02 m) stay at iteration 7 values, so the span is the only geometry change. Weights stay at [2, 1.333, 0.667, 0, -0.667, -1.333, -2], which is proportional to x at 28.6 per metre. This matches the outer sensors at ±2 and keeps the signal inside its ±2 limit. Gains are unchanged from iteration 7, so any change in result comes from the wider span. Expected result, not measured: oval completions hold near 14 of 20, slalom line_loss_events fall below 0.25, and the s-bend and slalom get their first progress above 0.3. If oval completions fall while line loss falls, the weights are too large for the wider span and need rescaling rather than a geometry change.
